subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should trusted hook-agent integrations get an explicit persistent session mode, or should /hooks/agent remain isolated-only with docs clarifying that sessionKey does not imply transcript continuity?
rationale: Current source proves the requested behavior is still missing, but accepting persistent hook sessions changes hook API/config surface and session routing security boundaries.

options.title: Accept explicit persistent mode
options.body: Review and land a narrow version of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 that keeps isolated as the default and gates persistence through existing hook auth and session-key policy.

options.title: Keep hooks isolated-only
options.body: Reject the linked PR direction and update docs to state that hook sessionKey is routing metadata rather than transcript continuity.

options.title: Design broader session identity first
options.body: Pause the linked PR and decide a wider trusted-hook identity and concurrency model before adding public config surface.

recommendation.title: Accept explicit persistent mode
recommendation.body: Review and land a narrow version of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 that keeps isolated as the default and gates persistence through existing hook auth and session-key policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter supplied the latest product/security direction on this exact issue and is the best available owner for the API boundary choice.
